elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at end of a term on 90 days' notice
elements.evidence: "M&I may not, during the Term, withdraw any of the Services ... upon providing ninety (90) days' prior written notice" — no end-of-term right is expressly preserved

reasons: All preferred elements are present: 30 days' written Customer convenience notice, no early-termination fee, an express pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, and removal of M&I's mid-Term Service-withdrawal (convenience) right.

Intent is not fully preserved: the balance of 11.1 was left untouched and now contradicts the edit — "The Termination for Convenience Fee shall apply to any early termination of this Agreement", "Fifty percent of the Termination for Convenience Fee shall be paid to M&I within thirty (30) days following the date of Customer's notice" and "The Termination for Convenience Fee shall not be subject to the limitations set forth in Section 13.4" are dangling mechanics for a fee that no longer exists.

The 10.2 edit is syntactically defective: "M&I may not, during the Term, withdraw any of the Services ... upon providing ninety (90) days' prior written notice" can be read as prohibiting withdrawal only when 90 days' notice is given; the trailing notice mechanic should have been deleted (e.g., "M&I may not, during the Term, withdraw any of the Services (other than the Core Services).").
"Estimated Remaining Value" in definition N is now an orphaned definition, though harmless.
Recommend a conforming clean-up: strike the three residual Termination for Convenience Fee sentences and the surviving 90-day notice tail in 10.2.
